newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stable, call remains high.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stable, call remains high.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were glued to Friday's levels on Monday, with call money quoted at relatively high levels of 2.88 to 3.06 percent bid at around 14.00 GMT. Dealers said most trades in call money were done at between 3.00 and 3.125 percent.
Some dealers said a continuing liquidity shortage could keep call rates at current high levels until the end of the year.

"Figures released by the central bank this morning showed that Friday's use of the secured loans facility was one billion guilders above Thursday's. Apparently, there is a shortage of money, which keeps call (money) high," one dealer said.
He said he would not be surprised if call rates remained at their current levels until the end of the year, but added there was also a possibility they could plunge on December 30 or 31.
"If many players conclude they have reached their goals for the year, they might suddenly start selling call money and cause a sudden drop in the rate," he said.
Dealers said most trades were done in call money and in deposits maturing immediately after the year-end.

This afternoon, the Dutch central bank will announce a new special advances pact, replacing the current 2.50 percent six-day facility. Dealers said they expected the rate of the new pact to be unchanged at 2.50 percent.
The guilder traded at 112.200/210 per 100 marks today, fractionally stronger than Friday's level of 112.250/650.
